A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of 98 VLMs, controlled MAD and CC12M experiments, embedding analyses and numerical simulations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds robustness experiments and fine-tuning results on densely captioned images.

M1.justification: The proposed measurements and underlying model procedures are retained. BRACE names the generic MOAD calculation already described in v2; the additional backbone and fine-tuning experiments do not introduce a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds CC3M training and fine-tuning on the Densely Captioned Images (DCI) dataset in Appendix F. These extend image-text data coverage, including dense captions, while retaining the existing downstream datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated VLM collection and comparator membership in the filtering and real/ideal/shifted-word comparisons are retained. The added experiments vary training conditions and model configurations without introducing another competing method.

E3.justification: Added protocols include ViT-S and sentence-wise caption removal in Figure 15, alternative dimension selection in Figure 12, and ten-epoch DCI fine-tuning with batch size 256 and learning rate 1e-5. These supplement existing protocols; the original settings and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: V3 substantially broadens robustness testing of the modality-gap explanation across backbone choice, caption-removal scheme and independent training data (Figure 15). Appendix F.6 additionally tests gap reduction in pretrained CLIP and SigLIP through dense-caption fine-tuning. Figure 12 checks separability under alternative dimension selection.

E5.justification: The three-seed MAD reporting, five-seed Appendix F.4 experiments and correlation significance reporting are unchanged. The added experiments introduce no new stated repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1-9 retain their results, while new robustness and fine-tuning outcomes materially expand the empirical evidence. In v3 Table 10, DCI fine-tuning reduces COCO RMG from 0.572 to 0.499 for CLIP and 0.623 to 0.562 for SigLIP. Their R@1 changes from 52.84 to 59.24 and 67.68 to 67.58, respectively; ImageNet accuracy falls from 66.75 to 65.13 and 75.61 to 73.87. These are newly reported experimental comparisons, not revisions to v2 scores.

T1.justification: The loss equations, modality-gap definitions and toy-optimum reasoning are retained. BRACE's equation in Appendix E.2 substitutes generic concept groups for MOAD's objects and attributes; v2 already explicitly allowed this use, so it restates existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's seven findings and conclusion retain the same substantive contributions concerning information imbalance, modality separation, object bias and logit entropy. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 narrows its interpretation to weak indications of negative correlation for some pretraining datasets. New Appendix G discusses limits from training scale and caption-removal variability, extending existing statistical caveats. Appendix F.6 tentatively attributes reduced transfer accuracy to distribution shift.

D1.justification: V3 adds an explicit project-code availability link and documents DCI fine-tuning hardware, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedule, warm-up and temperature cap. Existing implementation recipes are retained; these are additional reproducibility disclosures.

R1.justification: Appendix H adds a connection to partial multi-label learning, citing Xie and Huang, Struski et al., and Hang and Zhang. Urbanek et al. is added for DCI. The main positioning relative to prior modality-gap and object-bias research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording corrections, adds the conference header and BRACE terminology, and appends subsections on fine-tuning, limitations and partial multi-label learning. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figures 12 and 15 and Table 10, clarifies Figure 4's caption, and relocates several existing displays, including Figures 5 and Table 9. Existing plots largely retain their designs; v2 Figures 12-14 correspond to v3 Figures 13, 14 and 16.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens v2's real-data validation through targeted robustness checks and pretrained-model fine-tuning, while adding code-access information and clearer limitations. Table 10 usefully documents that shrinking the gap does not consistently improve downstream performance. These additions improve evidential coverage and qualification, but the limited statistical support for the gap-performance relationship and lack of large-scale intervention experiments remain.
